nodes.summary: A garbled, OCR-scanned FBI memorandum (circa 1970) from M. A. Jones to Mr. Bishop regarding Elvis Presley's visit to FBI Headquarters on 12-31-70 with Jerry Schilling, Sergeant Joe Clayton-like security staff, and Sheriff William Morris of Shelby County, Tennessee. It covers Presley's request to meet Director Hoover, arranged via Senator George Murphy and Congressman/Casper contacts; Presley's praise of Hoover and the Bureau, his anti-drug volunteer offer, his views on the Beatles and entertainers, his Junior Chamber of Commerce award, and his background. The memo notes no arrest record exists and recommends a letter from Hoover be sent.

nodes.title: OBSERVATION:
nodes.summary: An OCR-garbled FBI memorandum (M.A. Jones to Bishop, RE: Elvis Presley, dated around 1970) covers Presley's visit to the Bureau building and his selection by the Junior Chamber of Commerce as one of the ten outstanding men of 1970, with a Presley-requested letter from the Director recommended for approval. It also covers Senator George Murphy's call on Presley's behalf, his arranged meeting with the Bureau of Narcotics director, Presley's offer to help with the anti-narcotics drive, Bureau file notes on extortion attempts and a paternity matter, and his past public criticism.

summary: A 1959 FBI document (dated April 22, 1959) to the Army's Assistant Chief of Staff for Intelligence concerns an anonymous letter postmarked Canton, Ohio, March 11, 1959, sent to RCA Victor Records, claiming a plot to kill Elvis Presley, a Red Army soldier stationed in Germany. Presley's manager was advised; the Cleveland prosecutor declined extortion prosecution, and the writer was deemed mentally unstable. FBI Laboratory handwriting analysis found the note not identical to the writer's known handwriting. The text includes teletype transmittal details, lab worksheets, and file retention notes.

summary: Mostly garbled OCR text from a scanned 1950s document about Elvis Presley. It includes a Tribune-style letter from teenager Charlotte Jones (Dallas, Texas) defending Elvis as greater than George Washington, Tchaikovsky, and others, and criticizing adults and schools; an article by George Sokolsky reflecting on youth and popularity; and an FBI memo/airtel from the La Crosse, Wisconsin and Louisville, Kentucky field offices. The FBI material covers Presley's concert riots, police cooperation, Director J. Edgar Hoover's letter from a La Crosse newspaper man calling Presley a security danger and sexual threat to teens, and related correspondence. The remainder is illegible noise.

summary: The text is OCR-garbled scanned material, apparently a 1968 letter from the Southern Bell Telephone Company in Louisville, Kentucky, dated September 12, 1968. It describes a telephone operator's report that on September 6, 1968, a caller from Tennessee asked for an individual and gave a Louisville number. Company staff traced the call and found the last digits pointed to a pay telephone booth, indicating an attempt to defraud the telephone company. A second call was planned, and the rest of the text is largely unreadable noise.

title: 1 V - ;?:. !
summary: OCR-garbled 1968 FBI-style case document about a series of harassing hoax calls to the Lanning-Dunn Funeral Home in Louisville, Kentucky, placed from Memphis, Tennessee. Calls were traced to a residence on Street in Louisville, whose occupant was absent; the house appeared entered and its phone used. Police, the South Central Bell telephone company, and Louisville/Jefferson County authorities investigated; a suspect tied to the funeral home's radio-company owner's son is noted. The Kentucky US Attorney's office was consulted, and the matter was referred to local authorities.
